requirement.statement: The system SHALL classify parser-unsupported bash commands by deterministic risk before requiring human approval.

case.given: A bash command uses unsupported shell syntax but only performs readonly inspection commands
case.when: The parser cannot normalize the command
case.then: The evaluator SHALL allow the command when the classifier determines the command is low-risk readonly

case.given: A parser-unsupported bash command embeds a Python script that only reads files and prints diagnostics
case.when: The Python script has no obvious write, network, subprocess, or shell side effects
case.then: The evaluator SHALL classify it as low-risk readonly

case.given: A parser-unsupported bash command contains destructive, write, privilege, network-execute, or protected-config behavior
case.then: The evaluator MUST NOT silently allow the command

requirement.statement: The system SHALL normalize common low-risk shell command shapes before deciding that bash syntax requires human approval.

case.given: A bash command contains multiple top-level lines that each parse as supported command segments
case.when: The local permission evaluator parses the command
case.then: The evaluator SHALL treat the newline as a segment boundary and apply existing per-segment rules

case.given: A bash command invokes python through stdin heredoc with or without an explicit dash argument
case.when: The heredoc prefix is otherwise supported
case.then: The evaluator SHALL normalize the command to a python stdin segment such as `python3 -`
